headline: Man forced way into Arcadia home, killed teenage girl, police say
author: Iris Kwok, Richard Winton

paragraphs.text: Authorities said a teenage girl was killed after a man she was dating forced his way into a residence in Arcadia and shot her. The man then fled and attempted to take his own life in a shooting in Pasadena, officials said.
A witness told The Times there were multiple people who saw the Pasadena shooting, which took place on a sidewalk in broad daylight.
On Thursday around 11 a.m., Arcadia police responded to a call about a possible shooting in the 800 block of West Huntington Drive. The caller said a man was inside the residence and had fired a gun.
Officers arrived to find a girl with a gunshot wound, according to a statement Thursday afternoon from Arcadia police. She was pronounced dead at the scene.
“We heard a woman screaming,” Daisy Valdez told KTLA. “We heard her asking for an ambulance. It sounded like it was a mom for sure.”

By the time officers arrived, the man, identified by the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department as 20-year-old Paul Anthony Cruz Jr., had fled the scene, according to the statement. Arcadia police did not share the victim’s name.
The case remains under investigation and is being handled by the Sheriff’s Department Homicide Division, according to Arcadia police.
Authorities believe the man fled to Pasadena, where he attempted to take his own life about an hour later.
The Sheriff’s Department said Cruz was in a dating relationship with the victim. He had “forced entry” into the Arcadia location, according to the department.
Pasadena city spokesperson Lisa Derderian said the man was found with a self-inflicted gunshot wound in the city on Thursday about 12:30 p.m. and was transported to a hospital in critical condition.
Auto shop workers across the street from the incident told KABC that they heard a gunshot, then saw police handcuffing a man outside.

“We look out the window, there’s this guy, he’s laying face down on the floor. A couple seconds later, police officers show up and they close off the area,” said Michael Amini, manager at Alliance Auto Body Works, told the station.
The Sheriff’s Department said he shot himself as Pasadena Police Department officers were preparing to contact him. He remained in critical condition as of about 7 p.m.
Amini told The Times the neighborhood was “pretty busy” at the time of the shooting, and there were several other witnesses.
The suspect, who was being pursued by police, parked his car in the Petco parking lot, walked over to the sidewalk and pulled out the gun, Amini said.
After the shooting, Amini said, he saw the man lying face down. Police arrived about “five seconds” later, he said.
